title: Transfusion: Autoregressive Text and Diffusion Images

questions.question: What attention pattern does build_mask use for image patches inside one image span?
options: Bidirectional attention among patches in the same image, while text remains causal
Only each patch attending to its immediate predecessor
A fully bidirectional mask over every text and image token in the batch
No attention between image patches because diffusion is independent
questions.explanation: build_mask identifies image ranges between SEP_OPEN and SEP_CLOSE. Tokens in the same range attend to one another, while text-to-text positions obey j <= i.

questions.question: How does two_loss_step combine the text and image objectives?
options: It discards image loss whenever text loss is nonzero
It computes text_w*text_loss + img_w*img_loss as the total
It averages the two raw logits before either loss is computed
It uses only MSE for both modalities
questions.explanation: The returned total is weights['text_w'] * text_loss plus weights['img_w'] * img_loss. The two terms retain their modality-specific objectives.

questions.question: What does patch_to_vec([1,2,3,4]) return with HIDDEN=8?
options: A four-element normalized vector
Eight copies of the first patch value
[1,2,3,4,0,0,0,0], padding the short patch to HIDDEN
A scalar MSE value
questions.explanation: patch_to_vec keeps the four input values and appends max(0, 8-4)=4 zeros. It is a width adapter, not a normalization or loss function.

questions.question: What shape of training pair does make_dataset create by default?
options: Eight text tokens and a 16x16 RGB image
One scalar label and a list of patch IDs
A caption string and a variable-length audio waveform
24 Pair objects, each with caption [1,2,cls,3] and a 4x4 grayscale image
questions.explanation: make_dataset(24) creates 24 Pair instances. Each caption has four integer tokens and each image is a 4x4 list whose shade depends on cls.

questions.question: How does mse(a, b) normalize its squared error?
options: It sums squared differences and divides by the number of coordinates
It returns the largest coordinate error only
It computes cross-entropy over the two vectors
It divides by the batch size even when the vectors are empty
questions.explanation: mse sums (x-y)^2 over zipped coordinates and divides by max(1, len(a)). For normal non-empty vectors this is the mean squared error.

questions.question: Which comparison in the driver correctly characterizes Transfusion versus Chameleon?
options: Both use discrete image codes and only a masked diffusion loss
Transfusion keeps continuous image patches with a diffusion/flow loss while Chameleon uses discrete image tokens with NTP
Chameleon uses a frozen vision encoder and Transfusion has no text objective
Transfusion is text-only and Chameleon is the only multimodal model
questions.explanation: The driver contrasts continuous image patches plus an image flow/diffusion objective in Transfusion with Chameleon's discrete image tokens trained under next-token prediction.
